rulings.ruling: Ruling: second construction right (fixed: BUG-0085, the f8889.medical question now names the would-be dependents and the divorced-parents rule). The question for f8889.medical names expenses "of you, your spouse and your dependents", but line 15 also takes the expenses of "3. Any person who would be a dependent except that: a. The person filed a joint return. b. The person had gross income. c. You, or your spouse if filing jointly, are dependents of someone else" (i8889 p. 8, Line 15), and the p. 9 TIP treats a child of divorced or separated parents as the dependent of both; a filer answering the question as worded can leave those expenses off line 15 and overstate line 16 and the 20% tax.

rulings.model: The result is right in the ordinary cases, but a married filer age 55 or older who has family months and uses the last-month rule with self-only December 1 coverage gets $5,300 for self-only months because the married-family helper is false. The instructions say: "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3"; rule 2's treatment of December coverage as applying all year does not fit the program's use of actual family months in the changed-coverage chart.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year (owner ruling after Stage 16, reading 1) and amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change. The model says a married filer age 55 who uses the last-month rule with self-only December 1 coverage and earlier family months should not get $5,300, quoting the line 3 Note ("If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3"). Under the chosen reading i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2: "If the last-month rule (see Last-month rule, earlier) applies, you are considered an eligible individual for the entire year. You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year", so that filer is treated as self-only for every month and has no family coverage for the Note; line 7 is then $0, and the $1,000 is counted once, on line 3. The English states the chosen reading.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The months counted are every month treated as eligible, the owner's reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months (i8889 p. 7, Line 7 and the Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, "$1,000 × number of months eligible"; the Note on p. 5 keeps the additional amount off line 3 for every month once a married filer had family coverage at any time). 'You or your spouse had family coverage' is in the input: the family-months question tells a joint filer to "also count a month in which your spouse had family coverage while you were both eligible individuals" (i8889 p. 4, Line 1, "If you and your spouse are considered covered by a family HDHP, you are considered covered by a family HDHP"), so the gate's family test reads both spouses' coverage.
